claims.statement: The definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026, and EU importers or indirect customs representatives importing more than the single 50-tonne threshold of covered goods must seek authorised CBAM declarant status.
The CBAM Registry includes reporting and emissions-data functions, and its third-country installation module lets non-EU operators upload emissions once and share them with declarants.

Importers may base annual declarations on actual verified emissions or default values; the Commission's current timeline places first verification reports and certificate purchasing in 2027 for 2026 imports.

contrary_evidence: The Commission's own Registry already supports supplier-to-declarant emissions sharing, so a private product cannot be merely another submission form.
The 50-tonne threshold removes most low-volume importers from authorisation and reporting obligations and sharply reduces the addressable customer count.
Customs brokers, large consultancies, and enterprise trade-compliance platforms can bundle CBAM work into existing relationships.

economics.acquisition_route: Free annual-threshold and CN-code diagnostic, focused outbound to affected importers, then broker and accredited-verifier referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Modeled path: 250 importers at 2,500 PLN average monthly recurring revenue equals 7.5m PLN ARR; a 35% owner-cash margin would be 2.63m PLN/year and could accumulate more than 10m PLN in about four mature years without an exit
economics.founder_time: Up to 5 hours/day for a single-sector MVP; specialist reviews and onboarding must be contractorized before expanding sectors
economics.gross_margin_basis: Modeled 75-88% after document processing, secure storage, support, and limited emissions-specialist review
economics.payback: Target under 6 months because onboarding services partly fund acquisition; unvalidated against real sales cycles
economics.pricing: Modeled 1,200-4,500 PLN/month per importer plus 5,000-20,000 PLN onboarding based on supplier and customs-line complexity
economics.retention_or_repeat: Covered imports, supplier changes, quarterly certificate-price exposure, and annual declarations create recurring use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned mapping library across CN codes, supplier installations, evidence failure modes, verifier feedback, and accepted corrections
fingerprint.customer: EU importers above the CBAM mass threshold, initially Polish metal distributors and manufacturers importing iron, steel, or aluminium
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: CN-code and threshold diagnostic content, targeted importer lists derived from lawful public trade directories, and customs-broker or verifier referral partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier evidence portal, shipment-emissions matching engine, verification queue, and registry-ready exports sold as annual SaaS plus onboarding
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer or its customs/compliance provider pays on onboarding and monthly usage when covered shipments must be made declaration-ready
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A CBAM-covered customs line arrives without usable installation-level emissions, verification, or carbon-price evidence for the annual declaration

founder_fit: The product rewards quantitative data modeling, entity resolution, and anomaly detection rather than charisma-led selling.
Poland is a practical beachhead for an EU-wide regulation, while English-language workflows can extend the same product across the Union.
A narrow steel and aluminium pilot can be tested with synthetic and customer-provided shipment files within the founder's 5-hour daily limit.
risks: Incorrect CN-code or emissions treatment could cause material certificate costs, penalties, or customs disruption.
Regulatory simplification or better native Registry automation could compress the product's value.
Handling commercially sensitive supplier and emissions data creates security and contractual exposure.

structure.commercial_archetype: Cross-company regulatory data-exchange SaaS with implementation fees
structure.control_point: The auditable join from customs declaration line and supplier installation to verified embedded emissions and surrendered-certificate calculation inputs
structure.critical_dependency: Non-EU suppliers must provide sufficiently accurate emissions data and cooperate with accredited verification and Registry workflows

thesis: Build a workflow for Polish and nearby EU importers of iron, steel, aluminium, fertiliser, cement, hydrogen, or electricity that binds customs lines to non-EU installation emissions, verification status, carbon-price evidence, and annual declaration inputs. Importers pay to reduce the recurring coordination failure between purchasing, customs brokers, suppliers, verifiers, and the CBAM Registry rather than for generic carbon accounting.
title: CBAM Shipment-to-Emissions Evidence Exchange
uncertainties: The reachable count of Polish and EU importers above the threshold in the initial metal categories is not yet established.
The frequency with which suppliers fail to use the official third-country portal, and the cost of correcting that failure, is unknown.
Pricing, onboarding labor, liability allocation, sales-cycle length, and the modeled margin require validation with paid design partners.
